assessments.reasoning: Section 15.8.4 creates a capability for %Promise%, captures the declaration-instantiation completion, calls the capability’s rejection function on abrupt completion and starts the body otherwise. The returned completion carries that capability’s promise. The parameter binding steps in §10.2.11 admit the tested abrupt completion.

challenge.method: Trace the two branches and final completion. Force a benign throw in a default parameter initializer and compare it with a call supplying the parameter.
challenge.results: The initializer throw reaches the rejection branch, and success starts the body. Both branches return the newly created capability’s promise. This result concerns instantiation and does not specify timing of host work. The local Node.js v24.4.1 diagnostic agreed. Default-parameter throw rejected returned promise and skipped body; supplied value fulfilled.

limitations: The branch trace is controlling. A single local runtime check does not establish scheduler behavior or the outcome of every async expression.
